segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Keep the eyes open if that helps you feel present. Imagine the room as a quiet night market with many simple coordinates home.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Find five things you can see. Notice colour, edge, distance, shadow, or shine without needing them to be interesting.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Choose one visible object and study a detail you had not noticed before, like a tiny sign above a familiar stall.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft fabric rustling] Find four sensations of touch: feet on the floor, fabric on skin, air at the face, hands meeting an object.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Press gently into one reliable surface and feel it press back. Let that contact mark your location.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Listen for three sounds. Let each become a lantern placed somewhere on the map around you.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice two scents, or simply two qualities of the air if scent is faint: cool, warm, dry, fresh, familiar.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice one taste, perhaps neutral. You do not need to create a sensation that is not available.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] If any sense is inaccessible or uncomfortable, skip it and choose another visible or tactile detail. The map has many routes.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Say quietly: I am here, in this room, at this moment. Feel one breath arrive and leave while the market continues around you.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Choose the next small practical action: stand, drink water, open a window, send a message, or remain seated a little longer.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Let the imaginary lanterns fade. Keep the coordinates of sight, touch, sound, scent, and taste as you continue.
